title: Rumi for the Longest Night: Hope in Winter
subtitle: Eight Persian Sufi poems with English translation
yt_title: Rumi on Hope in Winter | 8 Persian Sufi Poems for Yalda Night (English Translation)
intro: This week Iranians celebrated Yalda, the longest night of the year, waiting together for the light to return.
Rumi wrote often about winter, hidden spring, and dry earth waiting for rain.
Here are eight passages of hope for dark seasons.

poems.name: Spring Is Hidden

lines.fa: پنهان بود بهار ولی در اثر نگر
lines.en: Spring is hidden, but look at what it does:

lines.fa: زو باغ زنده گشته و در کار آمده
lines.en: through it the garden has come alive and gone to work.

tafsir: We cannot see spring itself. We only see what it does.
Rumi says the same of grace, and of the Beloved.
Look for the signs: a garden waking, a heart softening.
What is hidden is not absent.

poems.name: Though Autumn Was Cruel

lines.fa: آنچ گل سرخ قبا می‌کند
lines.en: What the red-robed rose is doing,

lines.fa: دانم من کان ز کجا می‌کند
lines.en: I know where it comes from.

lines.fa: گرچه خزان کرد جفاها بسی
lines.en: Though autumn did many cruelties,

lines.fa: بین که بهاران چه وفا می‌کند
lines.en: see how faithful the spring is.

tafsir: Autumn strips the trees, and winter seems to win.
But the rose comes back, and Rumi knows its source.
Spring keeps its promise. It always has.
After a cruel season, faithfulness returns.

poems.name: You Are My Sky

lines.fa: تو آسمان منی من زمین به حیرانی
lines.en: You are my sky, and I am the earth, astonished

lines.fa: که دم به دم ز دل من چه چیز رویانی
lines.en: at what you make grow from my heart, moment by moment.

lines.fa: زمین خشک لبم من ببار آب کرم
lines.en: I am dry-lipped earth: rain down the water of generosity;

lines.fa: زمین ز آب تو یابد گل و گلستانی
lines.en: from your water the earth finds roses, and a rose garden.

tafsir: Here the lover is the earth and the Beloved is the sky.
Earth cannot make itself bloom. It can only wait, and ask for rain.
Rumi asks without shame: I am dry. Rain on me.
Asking for help is not weakness. It is how gardens begin.

poems.name: What Was Planted

lines.fa: زمین چه داند کاندر دلش چه کاشته‌ای
lines.en: What does the earth know of what you have planted in its heart?

lines.fa: ز توست حامله و حمل او تو می‌دانی
lines.en: It is pregnant by you, and only you know what it carries.

tafsir: In winter the field looks empty.
But seeds are already inside it, and the earth itself does not know what they are.
Many of us are like that in a dark season.
Something has been planted in us that we cannot yet see. Wait for it.

poems.name: A Thirsty Field

lines.fa: ماییم چو کشت ای جان سرسبز در این میدان
lines.en: We are like a field, dear soul, green in this open plain,

lines.fa: تشنه شده و جویان باران سحابی را
lines.en: grown thirsty, seeking the rain of the clouds.

tafsir: Even a green field gets thirsty.
Rumi does not pretend that faith removes need.
We stay green by staying open to the rain.
Thirst is not the end of hope. It is the shape hope takes while waiting.

poems.name: I Have Come Back

lines.fa: باز آمدم چون عید نو تا قفل زندان بشکنم
lines.en: I have come back like a new festival, to break the lock of the prison,

lines.fa: وین چرخ مردم‌خوار را چنگال و دندان بشکنم
lines.en: and to break the claws and teeth of this man-eating wheel of fate.

tafsir: This is the voice of new life returning, like Nowruz after winter.
Fate is pictured as a wheel with claws and teeth, grinding people down.
And something comes back, strong enough to break it.
Hope in Rumi is not soft. It has a hammer.

poems.name: Created Again

lines.fa: چه گویم مرده بودم بی‌تو مطلق
lines.en: What can I say? Without you I was utterly dead;

lines.fa: خدا از نو دگربار آفریدم
lines.en: God created me again, anew.

tafsir: Rumi does not soften it: I was dead.
And then, without any effort of his own, he was made again.
Many people who have come through a long winter of the soul know this feeling.
We do not always rescue ourselves. Sometimes we are simply created again.

poems.name: Do Not Grieve

lines.fa: اگر شد سود و سرمایه چه غمگینی چو من هستم
lines.en: If profit and capital are gone, why grieve, when I am here?

lines.fa: برآور سر ز جود من که لاتأسوا نمودستم
lines.en: Lift your head through my generosity, for I have told you: Do not grieve.

tafsir: Here the voice is the Beloved's, speaking to someone who has lost everything.
Do not grieve, it says, quoting the Quran.
What you lost was capital. What remains is the giver of all capital.
On the longest night, that is the hope: the light was never truly gone.

outro: Thank you for keeping watch with us through the long night.
